items.prompt: Identify two roles of government in an invented workshop that makes desks and hires carpenters.
items.canonical_answer: It produces goods through the desks and acts as an employer by hiring carpenters.
marking_guidance: Feature/example (1): Making desks is the goods-production role.
Distinct characteristic/example (1): Hiring carpenters is the employer role.

items.prompt: Identify two tangible outputs in an invented government workshop making desks and storage cabinets for schools.
items.canonical_answer: Desks and storage cabinets are goods produced by the government-controlled workshop.
marking_guidance: Feature/example (1): Desks are a tangible government-workshop output.
Distinct characteristic/example (1): Storage cabinets are a second tangible output.

items.prompt: Identify two services in an invented public district with clinic consultations and a library lending operation.
items.canonical_answer: Clinic consultations and library lending are services supplied by the district.

items.prompt: Identify two examples of direct government employment where an invented district itself hires librarians and carpenters, while delivery drivers work for a private contractor.
items.canonical_answer: The directly hired librarians and carpenters are government employees; the contractor’s drivers are not direct employees in this case.
marking_guidance: Feature/example (1): Directly hired librarians are government employees.
Distinct characteristic/example (1): Directly hired carpenters are government employees; private courier drivers are excluded.

items.prompt: Explain the error in calling a government-provided desk a free good because the school receives it without a purchase charge.
items.canonical_answer: The desk uses scarce resources with alternative uses, so it has an opportunity cost and is an economic good. No user charge does not establish a free good, and public-good status would require separate non-rivalry and non-excludability tests.
marking_guidance: Confusion (1): free at point of use mistaken for no opportunity cost. Boundary/test (1): scarce wood and labour establish an economic good.

items.prompt: Invented district arrangements: a government-controlled workshop makes desks and storage cabinets; a government clinic provides consultations and its library provides lending. The district directly hires carpenters, nurses and librarians. A private courier employs its own drivers to deliver supplies under a service contract. The library charges no lending fee but uses staff and premises resources. Identify two goods produced by government (2). Identify two government services (2). Explain why the librarians are direct government employees (2). Identify a production role and an employment role in the workshop (2).
items.canonical_answer: Desks and cabinets are goods. Consultations and lending are services. The district directly hires the librarians for its library duties, establishing an employment relationship. The workshop produces desks/cabinets and employs carpenters.
marking_guidance: Identification, separate points (2): desks (1), cabinets (1). Services (2): consultations (1), lending (1). Explanation (2): district directly hires (1), workers perform library duties under that relationship (1). Roles (2): goods production (1), hiring carpenters (1). Marks allocation 8.

items.prompt: Invented district arrangements: a government-controlled workshop makes desks and storage cabinets; a government clinic provides consultations and its library provides lending. The district directly hires carpenters, nurses and librarians. A private courier employs its own drivers to deliver supplies under a service contract. The library charges no lending fee but uses staff and premises resources. Describe government goods production, service provision and employment, each with one case detail (6). Explain how labour and other resources connect the workshop and library production roles to employment (4). Explain why the contractor’s drivers and the library’s lack of a user fee should not be used to misclassify direct employment or resource costs (4).
items.canonical_answer: The workshop produces tangible desks/cabinets; the clinic/library provide services; the district directly employs stated workers. Carpenters combine labour with wood/tools to produce goods, while librarians use labour with premises/records to provide services. The courier directly employs its drivers, so the government’s purchase of delivery is not direct hiring. Free lending still consumes staff and premises resources, so its opportunity cost is not zero.
marking_guidance: Context/data description (6): goods production (1), desks/cabinets detail (1); service provision (1), consultation/lending detail (1); employer (1), direct hiring detail (1). First explanation (4): carpenters supply labour (1), combine with tools/materials for goods (1); librarians supply labour (1), combine with premises/records for services (1). Second explanation (4): private courier is employer (1), service contract is not direct driver hiring (1); library resources remain scarce (1), no lending fee does not remove opportunity cost (1). Marks allocation 6+4+4=14.
